Bluegrass Renewable Fuels - Boston, KY
Executive Summary
RMP Hazard Assessment Information
Methane is considered a flammable/hazardous substance under 40 CFR part 68. Safety depends upon the manner in which we handle chemicals; combined with safety devices inherent in the design of this facility; and the training of our personnel. The facility produces methane in the form of biogas released from anerobic digestion of spent distillers grain. The biogas contains a high percentage of methane in it's raw form and is then upgraded to pipeline quality renewable natural gas. Release scenarios were discussed as part of the Process Hazard Analysis and a Worst Case Scenario was selected for Risk Management planning.
Worst Case Scenario: the 'biogas holder' vessel is ruptured at a pressure of 6.8" of water column releasing 22,251 pounds of biogas. While the biogas has a fraction of methane (approx 65%) the entire quantity was assumed to be methane to give a 1psi overpressure of 0.2 miles (RMP*Comp).
It is Bluegrass Renewable Fuel's (BRF's) intent to uphold industry standards in the design, construction and operation of the biogas system. It is our policy to adhere to all applicable federal, state, and local laws. BRF is required to and has implemented a Facility Emergency Action Plan. If an emergency was to occur, we have trained personnel and equipment ready for response in the event of a spill of hazardous materials. It is also our policy to notify the Boston, KY Fire Department (via the 911 system) and Nelson County Emergency Management in the event of an emergency.
BRF complies with EPA's Accidental Release Prevention Rule and will comply with all applicable state codes and regulations. BRF takes a systematic, proactive approach to evaluating chemical processes. Using this approach, the design, technology, operation and maintenance activities, emergency preparedness plan, training, process changes, and other elements that affect the covered process are all considered. By c

onducting thorough evaluations, accidental releases are prevented and the consequences of releases are minimized.
By fulfilling the required elements of the RMP standard, BRF intends to prevent releases of hazardous substances and minimize the effects of accidental releases, especially into locations that could expose employees, the community or the environment to serious hazards. Our management systems address each of the key features of a successful release prevention program including:
- Maintaining Process Safety Information: BRF maintains up-to-date technical information about safe operating limits of the process and associated hazard of the chemicals involved.
- Conducting Process Hazard Analysis: BRF performs technical analysis of the process in order to anticipate what might go wrong and recommend approaches to minimize the possibility and affect of such occurrences.
- Standard Operating Procedures: BRF has written technical and administrative procedures used to operate the facility safely.
- Training: BRF provides employees with necessary information to ensure safe operation.
- Mechanical Integrity: BRF ensures proper maintenance of process equipment on an on going basis.
- Management of Change: BRF analyzes changes in process equipment, procedures, and personnel to understand the impact of the change on the safe operation of the plant.
- Pre-Startup Safety Review: BRF ensures all necessary elements for operating a safe process are in place prior to introducing the hazardous chemical into the new or modified system.
- Compliance Audits: BRF conducts periodic evaluation and updating PSM/RMP implementation to ensure all elements are applied properly.
- Incident Investigation: BRF has procedures for investigating the causes of near-miss or accidental releases and developing measures to prevent future similar occurrences.
- Employee Participation: BRF maintains a philosophy and approach to incorporating the knowledge and experience of our employees from all fac

ets of operations regarding the covered process.
- Hot Work: BRF has a documented program for analyzing the need for and controlling the use of ignition sources within the facility.
- Contractors: BRF has policies and procedures for ensuring safe work practices of contractors at the facility and a systematic approach of communicating hazards which the contractor may be working on or near.
BRF and our employees are committed to meeting the standards prescribed by the RMP regulation. BRF does business and has specific accountabilities and controls to ensure that a high standard of accident prevention is met. BRF is adopting the stance of continuous improvement to always look for ways to increase safety and regulatory compliance.
